reasoning: Read both sides plus the compute hierarchy. FixTempBerendsenKokkos::end_of_step() (:134-142 and :157-165) removes/restores the bias with the group-wide hooks 'temperature->remove_bias_all_kk()' / 'remove_bias_all()' (identically in fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:139,142,162,165 and fix_temp_csvr_kokkos.cpp:130,133,159,162), while the CPU original loops per atom: src/fix_temp_berendsen.cpp:183-192 'temperature->remove_bias(i,v[i]); v[i][0] *= lamda; ...; temperature->restore_bias(i,v[i]);'. src/compute.h:151-159 declares remove_bias_all(), remove_bias_all_kk(), restore_bias_all(), restore_bias_all_kk() as EMPTY base methods, so a compute that implements only the per-atom form silently does nothing. I re-ran the scan over every compute that sets tempbias: exactly three implement remove_bias(int,double*) with no remove_bias_all - src/compute_temp_sphere.h:36-39, src/ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.h, src/BODY/compute_temp_body.h. ComputeTempSphere really is bias-capable (compute_temp_sphere.cpp:46-53 'tempbias = 1' when a bias compute is named, :344 ComputeTempSphere::remove_bias), and ComputeTempSphereKokkos adds nothing (compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp defines no remove_bias_all_kk; its calls at :55,:81,:129,:155 are to its OWN tbias, not overrides) while setting kokkosable = 1 (:35), so the kk branch is a no-op too. 'which' is set from exactly this flag (fix_temp_berendsen.cpp:124 'if (temperature->tempbias) which = BIAS;'), so the fix believes a bias is being handled while nothing happens. Nothing guards it either: FixTempCSLDKokkos::init() (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:103-104) is the only /kk thermostat that refuses BIAS outright, and KokkosLMP::warn_nonkokkos_compute only warns.
fix: Two acceptable routes. (a) Guard: in FixTempBerendsenKokkos::init() (and the temp/rescale/kk and temp/csvr/kk equivalents), after calling the base init(), detect a temperature compute that provides no group-wide bias hook and error out, e.g. keep a flag set by the three affected computes or check that the compute overrides remove_bias_all; the message should point the user at the non-kk fix. (b) Better: implement remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() (and the _kk variants where a device path exists) in compute temp/sphere, compute temp/asphere and compute temp/body by looping their per-atom remove_bias/restore_bias over the group, which also makes the existing non-kk branch of these fixes correct.

reasoning: Read all three pieces. (3) The style sets that bound to the GLOBAL Coulomb cutoff, not to the LJ one: pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long_kokkos.cpp:350 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_cut_coulsq,static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(cut_coulsq));' and init_one :385/:392 'cut_coulsq = cut_coulsq'. (4) CPU base src/YAFF/pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp:159-179 computes forcecoul2/prefactor2/erfc2 inside 'if (rsq < cut_ljsq[itype][jtype])' with NO cut_coulsq test, :191-193 adds 'ecoul += prefactor2*erfc2*factor_coul;' under the same cut_ljsq test, and fpair is '(forcecoul + factor_coul*forcecoul2 + factor_lj*forcelj)*r2inv'. In PairMM3Switch3CoulGaussLongKokkos::init_one() set the per-pair Coulomb bound to max(cut_coulsq, cut_ljsq[i][j]) for k_params(...).cut_coulsq, m_cut_coulsq[i][j] and d_cut_coulsq(i,j) (and replace the blanket deep_copy at :350 accordingly), then inside compute_fcoul()/compute_ecoul() wrap the Ewald block (:210-224 and :288-301) in 'if (rsq < cut_coulsq_kk) { ... }' so it is still cut at the true Coulomb cutoff, leaving the existing 'if (rsq < cut_ljsq_val && lj2_val > 0.0)' Gaussian block to fire out to cut_lj. reasoning: Mechanism verified end to end. MLIAPModelKokkos::set_k_coeffelem() (src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_kokkos.h:36-49) returns early only when model->coeffelem is null; otherwise it builds a Kokkos-backed copy with memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_coeffelem, tmp, nelements, nparams, ...), then does 'memory->destroy(model->coeffelem); model->coeffelem = tmp;'. create_kokkos for a 2d array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:180-196) smallocs only the row-pointer block and sets 'array[i] = &h_data(i,0)', i.e. array[0] points into Kokkos-owned storage; the matching destroy_kokkos (:271-281) correspondingly does 'data = TYPE(); sfree(array);' and never touches array[0]. Memory::destroy for a 2d array (src/memory.h:208-214) does 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' - so a second call would free() a pointer into a Kokkos allocation. Confirmed latent, and I checked the Cython side too rather than assuming: the only two call sites are one-shot constructor paths (src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_linear_kokkos.cpp:30 'if (args) set_k_coeffelem();' and src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:79-82 inside 'if (coefffilename)'), and grep over src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx and mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx finds no reference to coeffelem or set_k_coeffelem, so Python cannot trigger a second call either.
fix: Make the swap safe against repeat calls: in set_k_coeffelem(), replace 'memory->destroy(model->coeffelem);' with a check on whether coeffelem is already Kokkos-backed - e.g. keep a bool member 'coeffelem_is_kokkos' (false until the first successful call) and do 'if (coeffelem_is_kokkos) memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_coeffelem_old, model->coeffelem); else memory->destroy(model->coeffelem);', copying into the new view before releasing the old. Simplest correct alternative: keep the plain array as the single owner and only deep-copy into k_coeffelem, never re-pointing model->coeffelem.
